- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days; reduce initial values by 1–3% to align with observed mean reversion.
- Underestimate late in the horizon (last 5–10 days); increase final forecast values by 1–3% to account for momentum or policy-driven spikes.
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes (e.g., >60–70) — cap forecast at 10–15% above peak to avoid overreaction.
- Model tends to lag in capturing true peak values — add 1–2 days of lead time to peak forecasts to match observed timing.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >65% above 30-day average, reduce by 2–5% per day until convergence.
- Avoid overfitting to recent high values — if last 5 days are >65, reduce forecast by 1–2% to prevent runaway inflation.
- Use rolling 7-day average as a sanity check — if forecast deviates >5% from 7-day moving average, adjust downward.
